What We Do

Full-Service ABA Therapy Revenue Cycle Management

ABA therapy billing operates under some of the most complex payer rules in behavioral health. Session units, authorization limits, rendering vs. supervising provider billing, and payer-specific code preferences (CPT vs. H-codes) all vary by plan. PMEX manages every layer inside your existing practice management system.

CPT and H-Code Billing

97151 to 97158 CPT codes and H2019/H2012 H-codes billed per payer-specific requirements.

Authorization Tracking

Session unit authorizations tracked per patient per payer with renewal managed proactively.

Rendering vs. Supervising

Correct billing structure for BCBA supervision vs. RBT direct service per payer policy.

Telehealth ABA Billing

Modifier 95 and POS codes applied per state telehealth parity law requirements.

Unit Limit Compliance

Weekly and monthly unit limits tracked to avoid automatic denials at threshold.

Medicaid Waiver Billing

State Medicaid ABA waiver billing managed with correct provider type and service codes.

Common ABA Therapy Billing Problems

Each problem below is one PMEX resolves before it costs you revenue.

Authorization units exhausted mid-month with no renewal in place, sessions denied retroactively.

PMEX tracks authorization units per patient and initiates renewal before the threshold is reached.

CPT codes submitted to a payer that requires H-codes, generating systematic rejections.

PMEX maintains a payer-specific code preference matrix and applies CPT or H-codes per each payer contract.

Rendering provider billed incorrectly when a supervising BCBA should be on the claim.

PMEX confirms the correct rendering and supervising provider structure per payer policy on every claim.

Telehealth ABA sessions submitted without state-specific telehealth parity modifier.

PMEX verifies telehealth ABA coverage per state and applies the correct modifier and place of service code.

Unit limits exceeded in a week, generating automatic denials without any notification.

PMEX tracks weekly unit counts per patient and flags encounters approaching the authorized limit.

Medicaid waiver ABA claims submitted with wrong service code or provider type for the state.

PMEX manages state Medicaid waiver billing with correct service codes and provider type per state program.

Denial Management

Top Denial Patterns in ABA Therapy Billing

ABA practices lose 20 to 35 percent of revenue to authorization gaps, code mismatch errors, and unit limit violations. These three patterns dominate.

PATTERN 01

Authorization Expired, Sessions Denied Retroactively

6-month authorization covers 120 units per month. Month 7 sessions delivered without renewal. Commercial payer denies retroactively. $3,200 in session revenue denied with no appeal pathway without a new authorization covering those dates.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX tracks authorization expiration dates per patient per payer and initiates renewal 21 days before the current authorization ends, attaching updated treatment plan documentation and functional behavior assessment from the BCBA.

PATTERN 02

H-Code Rejected, Payer Requires CPT

Claim submitted with H2019 (behavioral health day treatment). Payer contract specifies CPT 97153 (adaptive behavior treatment). H-code rejected at clearinghouse. Revenue delayed and claim ages while resubmission is pending.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX maintains a payer-by-payer ABA code preference table and applies the correct code set for every payer. Claims are never submitted with a code type the payer does not accept.

PATTERN 03

Rendering Provider Error, Claim Denied

RBT delivers a direct therapy session. Claim submitted with the RBT as the rendering provider. Payer requires the supervising BCBA as the rendering provider with the RBT identified as the treating clinician in the notes. Claim denied for incorrect rendering provider NPI.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX confirms the correct rendering and supervising provider structure per payer policy before submission. BCBA NPI is applied as rendering provider on all payers that require supervision billing, with the treating clinician documented per the payer guidelines.

Questions

ABA Therapy Billing Questions Answered

CPT codes (97151 to 97158) are the AMA codes for adaptive behavior services. H-codes (H2019, H2012) are HCPCS codes used by some state Medicaid programs and commercial payers. We apply the correct code set per each payer contract.

We track authorized units per patient per payer per authorization period. When units approach the limit, we initiate the renewal process with updated treatment plan documentation before the authorization expires.

Yes, in most states with telehealth parity laws. We verify ABA telehealth coverage per state and per payer and apply the correct modifier and place of service code on qualifying remote sessions.

Billing structure varies by payer. Some require the BCBA as the rendering provider with supervision documented. Others allow the RBT to bill under their own NPI with a supervising provider modifier. We apply the correct structure per payer policy.

Yes. We manage state Medicaid waiver billing with the correct service codes, provider type enrollment, and documentation requirements for each state program.
